The test image shows a corn ear with:
- Exposed kernels (golden/orange) heavily darkened/blackened at base
- A large white-gray gall/mass at the top of the ear
- Black spore-like material coating much of the ear structure
- Husks dark and deteriorated

This strongly suggests smut disease. The white-gray bulbous structure at top that appears to be bursting with dark spores is characteristic of Common Smut. Let me confirm with a reference.

The reference shows a mature black smut gall on corn. The test image shows a larger ear infection with the classic Common Smut pattern: white-gray gall at top (immature, intact) and black spore masses below (mature, bursting). The golden kernels are still visible, surrounded by the dark fungal tissue — exactly the ear gall pattern of *Ustilago maydis*.
